title: MCP Tool Agent
description: Wire an agent to an external tool over MCP, so it can take real actions instead of just answering questions.

setup.title: Get your project on disk
setup.description: Same rule as always: this runs locally. Lyzr only comes in when it's time to actually create and run the agent.

scratch.label: Start from Scratch
scratch.sub: Empty repo, you wire the MCP server yourself

levels.title: Tool-Connected Agent
levels.desc: Give your agent a real action to take, not just a document to read.

missions.title: Mission 1 — Define the agent's job
missions.desc: Before wiring any tool, decide what this agent is actually for. Pick a model and describe its role clearly — the tool step depends on this being specific.

miniSteps.label: Choose your model
miniSteps.sub: Same trade-off as any agent: speed vs reasoning

miniSteps.label: Write the role
miniSteps.sub: One sentence: what job is this agent doing?

miniSteps.label: Write the goal
miniSteps.sub: What does success look like for this agent?

slots.label: goal
slots.placeholder: e.g. label and prioritize incoming issues

missions.codeTemplate:
# mcp_server.py already exposes tool endpoints — you don't touch that
from lyzr_adk import Studio

studio = Studio(api_key=API_KEY)

agent = studio.create_agent(
    name="MCP Tool Agent",
    provider={{model|tojson}},
    role={{role|tojson}},
    goal={{goal|tojson}},
    instructions="Use the connected tool when the user's request requires an action, not just an answer."
)

assist.tradeoffs: A vague role ("helper bot") makes the next mission's tool wiring ambiguous. A specific role ("GitHub issue triage assistant") makes it obvious which single tool call it needs.
assist.mistakes: Writing the goal as a personality trait ("be helpful") instead of an outcome ("label and prioritize issues") — Lyzr uses goal to steer tool-use decisions, not tone.
assist.docs: See Lyzr docs: Agent Studio > Tools > Overview for how tool connections attach to an existing agent.

missions.title: Mission 2 — Connect the MCP tool
missions.desc: mcp_server.py already exposes a working tool endpoint. Your job: point the agent at it and decide when it's allowed to call it.

miniSteps.label: Name the tool endpoint
miniSteps.sub: Which MCP tool this agent is allowed to call

miniSteps.label: Set the trigger condition
miniSteps.sub: When should the agent actually invoke it vs just answer in text?

slots.label: trigger_condition
slots.placeholder: e.g. only when user asks to take an action

assist.tradeoffs: A tight trigger condition means fewer accidental tool calls but more "I can't do that" responses. A loose one means more automation but more risk of unintended actions.
assist.mistakes: The #1 MCP mistake: forgetting the agent needs the trigger condition in plain language, not code — Lyzr's model decides when to call the tool based on how you describe the condition, not a regex.
assist.docs: See Lyzr docs: Responsible AI guardrails before letting any tool-connected agent run unattended in production.

finalize.goalTemplate: {{goal}} Use the connected tool at {{tool_endpoint}} when: {{trigger_condition}}.
finalize.testMessage: What can you do, and what tool do you have access to?
